title.title: The Thief on the Cross
title.subtitle: Bible Readings — Chapter 110 — A Scripture Narrative

s01-luke-23-32-33.text: And there were also two other, malefactors, led with him to be put to death. And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.
s01-luke-23-32-33.note: "On either side one, and Jesus in the midst." DA 751.4: His place between the thieves was to indicate that He was the greatest criminal of the three. Isaiah 53:12 fulfilled: numbered with the transgressors.

s02-luke-23-39.text: And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.
s02-luke-23-39.note: Both men at first railed on Him (Matt 27:44). DA 749.3: one under his suffering only became more desperate and defiant.

s03-luke-23-40-41.text: But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation? And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.
s03-luke-23-40-41.note: "We indeed justly ... but this man hath done nothing amiss." He owns his guilt and confesses Christ's innocence in one breath. DA 749.3: he had seen and heard Jesus, and had been convicted by His teaching.

s04-luke-23-42.text: And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
s04-luke-23-42.note: He asks to be remembered when Christ comes into His kingdom, a day yet ahead. DA 750.1: the helpless, dying soul casts himself upon a dying Saviour.

s05-luke-23-43.text: And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
s05-luke-23-43.note: DA 750.2 renders it: "Verily I say unto thee today, Thou shalt be with Me in paradise." DA 751.2: the dark cloud that seemed to enshroud the cross was pierced by a bright and living light.

s06-luke-19-12.text: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
s06-luke-19-12.note: Christ's own parable: the kingdom is received far away, and the King returns with it. The thief asked for that day.

s07-matthew-27-29.text: And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!
s07-matthew-27-29.note: The world crowned Him with thorns. Every sign said His kingdom had failed.

s08-matthew-27-42.text: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.
s08-matthew-27-42.note: "Himself he cannot save." DA 750.3: while the leading Jews deny Him, and even the disciples doubt His divinity, the poor thief calls Jesus Lord.

s09-revelation-2-7.text: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God.
s09-revelation-2-7.note: Scripture defines Paradise for us: where the tree of life grows.

s10-revelation-22-1-2.text: And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
s10-revelation-22-1-2.note: The tree of life grows by the river that proceeds from the throne of God. Paradise is where the Father's throne is.

s11-2-corinthians-12-2-4.text: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven. ... How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
s11-2-corinthians-12-2-4.note: The third heaven and paradise are the same place in Paul's account: caught up, not down.

s12-1-corinthians-15-3-4.text: For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:
s12-1-corinthians-15-3-4.note: Died, buried, rose the third day. Friday night and the Sabbath He lay in Joseph's tomb.

s13-john-20-17.text: Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.
s13-john-20-17.note: Sunday morning: "I am not yet ascended to my Father." DA 751.3: He Himself did not go that day to Paradise. He slept in the tomb.

s14-titus-1-2.text: In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;
s14-titus-1-2.note: God cannot lie. Christ's words to the thief and to Mary stand together, once the comma stands where He put the emphasis.

s15-zechariah-9-12.text: Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee;
s15-zechariah-9-12.note: "Even to day do I declare": the day the promise is spoken, not the day it is kept. DA 751.3: on the day of the crucifixion, the day of apparent defeat and darkness, the promise was given.

s16-deuteronomy-30-19.text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:
s16-deuteronomy-30-19.note: "This day" again marks the day of speaking. Moses calls heaven and earth to witness the words spoken now.

s17-john-14-3.text: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
s17-john-14-3.note: "I will come again, and receive you." The meeting is fixed at His coming, not at our death.

s18-1-thessalonians-4-16-17.text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
s18-1-thessalonians-4-16-17.note: The dead in Christ rise first. The thief is among them, and so shall he ever be with the Lord.

s19-revelation-22-12.text: And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.
s19-revelation-22-12.note: The reward comes with Him. The thief's paradise and ours arrive on the same day.

s20-ecclesiastes-9-5-6.text: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten. Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.
s20-ecclesiastes-9-5-6.note: The dead know not any thing. The thief has had no waiting to endure.

s21-psalm-146-4.text: His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish.
s21-psalm-146-4.note: In that very day his thoughts perish. His next thought will be the voice of Christ calling him.

s22-john-11-11.text: These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
s22-john-11-11.note: Christ's own word for death is sleep, and His errand is to awake. To the thief, paradise will seem to come that very day.

s23-ephesians-2-8-9.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
s23-ephesians-2-8-9.note: No baptism, no works, no restitution possible. Only faith, and Christ received him fully. DA 751.2: it is His royal right to save unto the uttermost all who come unto God by Him.

s24-luke-23-42.text: And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
s24-luke-23-42.note: The same Saviour hears the same prayer today. "Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom."
